failure_modes.cause: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution (EAS) byproducts or oligomers precipitate on PFA walls due to long residence time (12.8 min) and low Reynolds number (Re=23) laminar flow, leading to blockage.
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement periodic back-flushing protocol and add 0.1% surfactant to feed; monitor dP for gradual increase.

failure_modes.cause: Insufficient mixing in the quench stage (laminar regime) fails to rapidly neutralize the electrophile, allowing secondary reactions or exothermic decomposition post-reactor.
failure_modes.mitigation: Install static mixer in quench line; validate quench efficiency via inline IR spectroscopy for residual electrophile.

failure_modes.mode: BPR Valve Failure to Open (Stuck Closed)
failure_modes.cause: Mechanical failure or crystallization of salts on the BPR seat prevents pressure relief, causing system pressure to exceed design limits (1.5 bar) and potentially rupture fittings.
failure_modes.mitigation: Install redundant pressure relief valve (PRV) set at 1.2 bar upstream of BPR; use heated BPR to prevent crystallization.

single_points_of_failure: BPR Valve — blockage or failure stops flow control
Single Pump — failure halts entire process
validation_experiments: Long-duration stability test: Run reaction for 24 hours at Q=0.83 mL/min; monitor pressure drop (dP) for >10% increase indicating fouling.
Quench efficiency validation: Spike reactor outlet with known electrophile concentration; measure conversion to quenched product using inline HPLC/IR.
BPR functional test: Simulate blockage downstream of BPR; verify PRV opens at 1.2 bar and system depressurizes safely.
